summary: The Journey of Cassini-Huygens is an informative story told from the perspectives of the Cassini orbiter and Huygens probe as they travel to Saturn to explore its atmosphere, rings, and moon, Titan, before ultimately self-destructing. Within this story framework, we explain the specific instruments attached to Cassini-Huygens so that it could observe Saturn and its moons, the components of both probes, and the procedures the probes used to collect data. To create narrative interest, we present Cassini and Huygens as two "people" who are at odds with each other, despite being physically attached to each other. As their mission to Saturn continues, they slowly begin to develop a friendship. By interspersing accurate information regarding the Cassini-Huygens mission within a traditional narrative structure, we allow school-aged children to learn about the space probes' role in collecting information about planets in a fun and engaging way.
details:
The project is divided into these sections.

  1. Cassini’s POV - Launch of Cassini-Huygen from Cape Canaveral (October 15, 1997)
  2. Cassini’s POV - Venus Flyby #1 (April 26, 1998)
  3. Huygen’s POV - Earth Flyby (August 20th, 1999)
  4. Cassini’s POV - Observation of Asteroid 2685 Masursky (January 23, 2000)
  5. Cassini’s POV - Jupiter Flyby (December 20, 2000)
  6. Cassini’s POV - Saturn Orbit Insertion (July 1, 2004)
  7. Huygen’s POV - Cassini-Huygen Detach (December 25, 2004)
  8. Cassini’s POV - Huygens Descent Into Titan and Observations (January 1, 2005)
  9. Cassini’s POV - Discovery at Enceladus, Saturn’s moon (October 28, 2015)
  10. Cassini’s POV - Storm Chokes on Its Own Tail (2013)
  11. Cassini’s POV - The Final Transmission (2017)
projectRefs: An Introduction to the Design of the Cassini Spacecraft - Curt A. Henry (JPL)
